records.summary: 1.Hostile Creatures: •Saltwater Crocodiles: Ambush predators that attack from beneath the water. Once they grapple a target, they drag it underwater. •Poisonous Snakes: Venomous snakes coil in the trees and attack anyone disturbing their territory. A failed Dexterity saving throw (DC 12) results in 2d6 poison damage. •Mangrove Apes: Highly territorial and aggressive, these apes travel in small groups. They throw debris or attack with makeshift weapons. •Giant Crabs: These creatures hide beneath the mud and water, snapping at those who come too close. Their powerful claws can deal massive damage and crush armor.

1.Treacherous Reefs: •Ships traveling through coral reefs must make Dexterity (Vehicle Handling) checks (DC 14) to avoid grounding. Failure results in 2d10 damage to the ship and potential delays. 2.Sudden Eruptions: •Active volcanoes erupt without warning. Players in the area must succeed on Dexterity saves (DC 15) to avoid lava flows or falling debris.

1.Quicksand-Like Patches: •Certain areas of mud act like quicksand. Characters stepping into these must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 13) to avoid sinking. Once trapped, they must make a Strength check (DC 15) to escape, or allies can assist. 2.Leech Swarms:

1.Travel Pace: •Slow: 2 miles per hour •Normal: 1 mile per hour •Fast: ½ mile per hour (increased exhaustion risk) 2.Navigation Difficulty: •Due to shifting waterways and undergrowth, make Wisdom (Survival) checks every 2 hours to avoid becoming lost (DC 15). 3.Random Sinking: •For every hour spent traveling, roll a d6. On a 1, the ground beneath a character sinks, requiring a Dexterity saving throw (DC 13) to leap clear or become restrained in mud.

•Short Rest: Characters can find dry patches on elevated roots or within hollowed-out trees to rest. These places are risky, as predators often lurk nearby. Thereʼs a 1-in-4 chance of encountering a predator or danger during a short rest. •Long Rest: Long rests in the mangrove swamp are difficult, as the constant moisture, insects, and predators make it hard to relax. Characters sleeping without proper shelter must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) or gain 1 level of exhaustion •Long Rest (Continued): To avoid exhaustion, players must build a waterproof shelter, find an elevated spot safe from predators, or use magical protection. A successful Wisdom (Survival) check (DC 15) ensures the camp remains undisturbed. Roll a d20 each hour during the rest—on a roll of 5 or lower, an encounter or environmental hazard disturbs the camp (such as rising water, a crocodile, or a swarm of mosquitoes).
Short rests require finding an air pocket or a dry chamber. Roll a d20; on a 5 or lower, an encounter with a lurking predator or hazardous event occurs, interrupting the rest.

1.Leeches: Characters wading through swamp water may attract leeches. After 1 hour in water, each character rolls a Constitution saving throw (DC 12). On a failure, they lose 1 HP every hour until treated. 2.Quicksand Pockets: •A creature that steps into quicksand sinks 1 foot per round and must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check (DC 14) each round to pull free. Other characters can assist, reducing the DC to 10. 3.Diseases: •Swamp Rot: After prolonged exposure, characters roll a Constitution saving throw (DC 15). On a failure, the character suffers -2 to Constitution until cured with magic or medicine. •Bog Fever: Caused by bites from infected insects; symptoms include fatigue and fever. The player rolls a Constitution save (DC 13) each morning; two consecutive failures result in the poisoned condition. 4.Noxious Geysers: Swamp gases can ignite or explode. If a fire spell or open flame is used, roll a d20. On a roll of 5 or lower, a gas pocket ignites, causing 3d6 fire damage in a 10-foot radius.

records.proposedName: Echo Feedback System (for Relic or Technomancy Exposure)
records.summary: Technomantic devices sometimes contain embedded psychic echoes from the pre-Fracture age— memories, fragments of code, or divine impressions.

•Player performs a Divination Check (Insight or Religion + Wisdom). •On success (DC 15), GM provides an omen or cryptic truth about a question, event, or character. •On failure, the gravity stones give a false positive, a confusing or misleading omen.
This mechanic simulates the ever-present threat of gravitational instability caused by shifting Gravity Wells.
Mystic Skywalkers use gravity-reactive stones to simulate "fate shifts" and reveal insights.
If adventurers enter close orbit of a major Gravity Well (i.e. inside 500 ft), apply one of the following environmental modifiers:

•Vertical Zones: Divide combat arenas into up, middle, and down layers; characters must climb, leap, or fly to change zones. •Falling Is Damage: Falling into the sky counts as failing a check—unless players use tether lines, spells, or Gravi-gear. •Inversion Effects: Some spells or projectile attacks may behave unpredictably in shifted gravity (GM discretion or add +2 to the difficulty to target in unstable fields).

Every 4 hours, characters in unprotected areas must make Constitution saving throws (DC 13) to avoid respiratory issues, hearing loss, or gaining levels of exhaustion from prolonged exposure. ---

records.proposedName: Avoiding Toxic Spills and Chemical Hazards
records.summary: - Toxic spills and waste pools require Constitution saving throws (DC 15) every 10 minutes to avoid inhaling fumes or exposure effects, which can result in 1 level of exhaustion or temporary poisoning. ---

Certain areas may have pools of toxic waste or spilled chemicals. Characters who touch or fall into these pools must succeed on Constitution saving throws (DC 15) or take 2d6 poison damage and risk long-term exposure effects.

- Drones or industrial robots malfunction, moving unpredictably and sometimes becoming aggressive. Players within reach must make Dexterity saves (DC 15) to avoid damage from random swings or weaponry.

records.proposedName: Emphasize the Dangers of Machinery and Pollution
records.summary: Machinery malfunctions, toxic fumes, and chemical spills keep players on edge. Create tense moments where they must dodge equipment or find safe pathways to navigate through hazardous areas.

Workers or technicians may be hostile or defensive, depending on the situation. Characters may encounter workers who are resistant to outside interference, requiring Charisma (Persuasion) checks (DC 14) to gain cooperation.

Highly flammable substances and open flames are common. Any fire or explosion hazard nearby requires Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid 3d6 fire damage if ignited by a stray spark or malfunction.

records.proposedName: Fungal or Bacterial Contamination in Moist Areas
records.summary: - Poorly maintained areas may harbor harmful bacteria or mold. Characters must make Constitution saving throws (DC 13) to avoid minor poisoning or infection, which reduces Constitution by 1 temporarily.

Moving cranes, conveyor belts, and automated machinery can pose serious risks. Characters near these machines must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) every 10 minutes to avoid being hit by moving parts, risking 2d6 bludgeoning or slashing damage.

- Powerful magnets within some equipment can pull metal objects toward them unexpectedly, disarming characters or drawing them into machinery. Dexterity saving throw (DC 15) to avoid losing gear or taking 1d6 damage.

Industrial areas are frequently patrolled by security systems, drones, or guard robots. Characters entering restricted areas must make Dexterity (Stealth) checks (DC 15) to avoid detection or risk triggering security alarms.

- Characters moving near active machinery must make Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) to avoid entanglement, slipping, or sudden machinery movement. Failure may result in minor injuries (1d6 bludgeoning or slashing damage). - Crossing conveyor belts requires Dexterity saving throws (DC 13) to avoid getting pulled into machinery, which could result in entrapment or minor damage.

Valuable resources like refined chemicals, rare alloys, or high-energy components are often located in restricted areas. Accessing these requires Intelligence (Investigation) checks (DC 15) to find safe paths and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks (DC 14) to avoid setting off alarms. ---

records.proposedName: Rogue Scavengers and Black Market Dealers
records.summary: Industrial zones often attract scavengers or dealers looking to obtain parts illegally. They may offer trades, information, or try to steal valuable resources. Characters may need to make Wisdom (Insight) checks (DC 13) to determine their trustworthiness.

- Pipes and valves carrying high-pressure steam or chemicals may suddenly release, causing burns or knocking characters back. Dexterity saving throw (DC 14) to avoid 2d6 fire damage or being pushed 10 feet.

Old or poorly maintained structures in industrial zones are prone to collapse. Characters navigating these areas must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) to avoid falling debris, which may cause 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

Poor air quality and fumes from chemical processing affect anyone without protective gear. Characters in these zones must make Constitution saving throws (DC 14) every hour or gain the poisoned condition for 1d4 hours.
